#   sentence <TAB> sem (the chosen reading's pretty-printed term, verbatim) <TAB> verdict <TAB> evidence
# verdict = correct | wrong | uncertain. CORRECT = the reading faithfully expresses the sentence's
# meaning in the document; several readings may be faithful (cross-lexicon twins can render
# identically), and choosing any faithful one is correct. WRONG = the structure or a word sense
# contradicts the meaning. `uncertain` scores as UNADJUDICATED (excluded from the gate's
# denominator, reported; must be 0 on the tracked replay).
# **THE OBJECTIVE IS THE MOST APPROPRIATE READING** (maintainer, 2026-08-13). This ledger asks
# "is the chosen reading faithful", which is necessary but not the goal. The goal is the same one
# the skeleton pins serve at the structural level: establish, per sentence, WHICH READING IS THE
# RIGHT ONE — and then use that as the goal post the processing is adjusted to reach. A reading
# that is faithful-but-weaker is not the target; recording it as `correct` and stopping loses the
# signal that a better reading existed and was not chosen.
# So when several readings are faithful, say which is BEST and why, in the evidence. Then the
# question for the pipeline becomes mechanical:
#   * best reading NOT in the forest      → a coverage defect (lexicon, cap, tokenisation)
#   * best reading in the forest, not chosen → a selection defect (presentation, ranker, prompt)
# Both are fixable, and each fix is measurable against the same goal post. That loop ran four
# times on 2026-08-13 — the frozen sense-rank draw, the hyphen-joined multiword, the entry-counted
